qa.question: Can you evaluate recent management changes and elevation of  Doug and Troy to co-presidents, and what this means for leadership development and your tenure as CEO?
qa.answer: Marianne is exceptional individual. Board made decision to create two co-presidents to prepare them for more at company. Hasn't changed timetable. Marianne decided she'd rather retire than stay, result of knowing about succession plans. No mystery.

qa.question: How do you judge sustainability of investment banking and markets strength, and how risk-on are the various businesses?
qa.answer: Investment banking fees historically fine but not super peak, had room to come up. Some pull forward happened, large deals  contributed meaningfully. Pipeline quite robust; high-profile activity seems encouraging more activity. Markets elevated for time; equities exceptionally strong this quarter with highly dynamic conditions. Separation between fixed income up 6% and equities up 86% year-over-year.

qa.question: Can you discuss progression toward 15% retail market share target and how higher-for-longer rates impact pace of market share gains?
qa.answer: Wholesale deposit growth strong this quarter and first half, outperforming expectations due to franchise strength, winning deals, and lending environment particularly BFI space and data center stuff. Consumer expecting low single-digit growth, unchanged expectation, balance between  robust net new checking accounts and yield-seeking flows. View that 15% will be outcome of executing strategy across components from primary bank relationships, branch expansion, deepening product-value proposition.

qa.question: Where are we in the investment cycle for branch build-out, AI investments, and banker hires, and how does this play into operating leverage outlook?
qa.answer: Complete continuation of what we've been doing for years. Shouldn't expect any change. Power of franchise is such that able to aggressively invest for future generating returns and solidifying competitive position while delivering exceptional current returns. Would be true delivering 15%, 16%, 17%  returns. When delivering these types, firing on all cylinders.

qa.question: Can you talk about drivers of upward revision to NII ex-Markets from $95 billion to $96.5 billion and cadence in Q3, Q4, and exit rate?
qa.answer: Biggest single factor is deposit balances across wholesale and consumer, overall quantum and mix shift in favor of slightly higher margin. Rates higher than previously guided in short and back end. Sensitivity a little more than EAR suggests due to consumer betas outperformance, disproportionately in front end. Increase as function of higher rates but most is balances overall.

qa.question: Markets NII guided higher even though rate outlook higher. What are drivers, balance sheet mix?
qa.answer: Markets NII actually liability sensitive. Higher rates would expect it down; instead forecast up. Difference is changes in balance sheet composition, expecting lower finance non-interest-bearing assets in second half. One balance sheet unit drives number quite a bit, can overwhelm rate effect. Also increased equity allocation to CIB this quarter moves some equity out of corporate into CIB; markets NII moving out of NII ex-Markets into markets NII, about $150 million not expected to offset on bottom line.
